id.description: Filesystem-safe slug, matches this file's basename. Assigned once at pack creation and never changed even if `name` is later edited -- everything else (rules, tree.json, patches, ini attribution, update diffing) keys off this.

phase.description: Coarse install-SEQUENCING bucket only. NOT display order (see tree.json) and NOT a substitute for `rules`.

selections.description: Maps installer step/group id to the array of selected option ids, so install can run headless with no interactive prompts.

updatePolicy.description: exact pins to a specific fileId/version/hash captured at authoring time -- those fields are REQUIRED when this is exact. prefer keeps that same pin but permits the fallback the author asked for: if the pinned file was archived or deleted upstream, install takes the mod's newest file instead. latest deliberately omits the pin: the resolver fetches whatever the source currently reports as newest at install/update time, independent of the pack's own `revision`, and there is no pack-declared identity to require or verify against. Not every provider can honor `exact` for every mod (a mod author may not keep old files available at all), so `exact` is a request the resolver attempts, not a structural guarantee this schema can enforce on its own.

resolution.description: api = Premium download-link generation available. browser = free-tier manual click-through, matched back to the archive by fileName/size after the fact -- both are equally capable of `exact` or `latest`; the split here is about how the file gets fetched, not which version.

fileId.description: Required when updatePolicy is exact or prefer. Omit entirely for latest -- there is no fixed fileId to pin.

version.description: Required when updatePolicy is exact or prefer.

sha256.description: Required when updatePolicy=exact. Compared against the actually-resolved file at install/update time -- see the parent spec doc for mismatch handling.

md5.description: Nexus publishes an md5 of the archive and never a sha256, so an imported Nexus source carries its digest here. It is what the server SUPPLIED about the archive -- never a claim about the installed folder, which we hash ourselves and which would attest nothing the collector did not already have. Informational only: an md5 does not satisfy the sha256 requirement of an exact pin, so a source with only md5 is exported as prefer.

resolution.description: No public API exists for this provider -- always browser-redirect, for both exact and latest.

version.description: Required when updatePolicy=exact. Best-effort even then -- LL mod authors don't reliably keep old file versions attached, unlike Nexus.

resolution.description: Capability unverified as of this schema version -- do not assume `api` is available; treat as `browser` unless GMM's provider-capability table says otherwise.
Resolved via Steamworks subscribe / steamcmd, NOT an HTTP fetch.

version.description: Always unknown ahead of time -- Steam has no discrete file-version identity to pin, and no per-file hash exposed the way Nexus/LoversLab/ModPub downloads have. This is a real platform limit, not a gap in this schema: you either get whatever is currently live, or nothing.

updatePolicy.description: Always latest -- exact pinning is not offered as an option here because the platform cannot honor it. Do not present this as a curator choice for Steam Workshop mods.

sourceEmbedded.description: A mod whose own files ship inside the archive under files/<root>/. The one provider with no external origin: a manual or unrecognised-source mod has no download identity, so exporting it means carrying the bytes. Every payload file is listed with its size and sha256, and install verifies both before writing anything.

resolution.description: Resolved from the archive itself - there is nothing to fetch.

root.description: Directory inside files/ that holds this mod's payload.

fileCount.description: Number of entries in files[]; a mismatch means the listing was edited.

path.description: Path relative to root. Never absolute, never containing '..'.

updatePolicy.description: Always latest, same reasoning as Steam Workshop: the content is whatever THIS revision of the pack carries, so there is no separate version identity to pin. The per-file sha256 list above is the integrity pin, verified at install time.
